replies.author: @richardburden6035
replies.text: I'm in northern Virginia, USA. My meter measures 0.10 microsieverts per hour. That.s 2.4 per day,  876.6 per year. Still less than 1 milliSv per year, well below the world average background of 2 mSv, if my meter is right. .045 microSV per hour  is radiation starvation! But I suspect these cheap meters are not measuring the alpha particles. Cesium-137 does not emit alpha particles. Alpha particles come from naturally-occurring radioactive substances--uranium, thorium and their daughters, such as radium and radon, as well as products of neutron capture by uranium, including the much-maligned plutonium. The dose makes the poison. The boar meat is safe to eat, although perhaps not every day and without measuring it. Unlike the butterflies, we can measure the contamination and not spend our whole lives in the most contaminated spot, eating only the most contaminated vegetation, and thereby be selected by people trying to prove that a nuclear accident is so terrible that the people who built or operated or owned the reactor should be executed.

replies.author: @WhereonEarth4K
